Baseline treadmill exercise time: the text gives 1 min and 4 s for the baseline Bruce protocol test, whereas supplementary Table S2 prints a Modified Bruce exercise time of 258 s (4 min 18 s) under the 5.14.2020 column; the text instead places a 4 min and 18 s Modified Bruce test at the first outpatient follow-up after hospitalization. The protocol labels differ, but both sources give the baseline (5.14.2020) treadmill time with different numbers, so the text baseline time is review-only (source conflict) and the date of the 258 s test is disputed; do not choose either.

After discharge the text lists Vitamin D3 (changed from Vitamin D2) and Bystolic, but supplementary Table S1 lists Vitamin D2 50,000 IU once a week with Bystolic under 06.12.2020, after the 28 May 2020 discharge. Source conflict on the vitamin D form at the same post-discharge time; the Vitamin D3 item is review-only.

Text lab values at the first visit (creatinine 5.08, eGFR 14, carbon dioxide 18, urea nitrogen 176) equal the 14 May 2020 Table 1 row, but the text sentence states no date or table link, so the text and table items are kept separate and not merged.
Likewise the text eGFR 47 / creatinine 1.80 after follow-up (percent changes from discharge) equals the 11 June 2020 table row, but no date is stated in the text sentence; not merged.

Causes are hedged and not asserted: medication-induced volume depletion and renal toxicity as the systemic insult, torsemide and Entresto contributing to volume depletion, polypharmacy, and chest pain and shortness of breath "could have been due to" decompensated heart failure with volume overload or cardiac ischemia due to volume depletion (an "or" statement that asserts neither).
The infusion solution is printed as "0.045% saline" in the Discussion but as 0.45% sodium chloride elsewhere; treated as a print artefact and 0.45% used.

The text reports 6 L of intravenous fluids during hospitalization with the first 2 L before the initial arterial blood gas; supplementary Table S2 and Figure 2 print cumulative IV fluids up to 8 L. The article does not state whether the cumulative total includes the 2000 mL given in clinic on day 7, so no conflict is recorded.

Day 4 text says "insulin" was discontinued while the baseline list names Humalog and Lantus; the items are not mapped to each other. The Table 1 description for 22 May 2020 ("Up to this point, all medications except Vitamin D2 were discontinued") is the only source for carvedilol being stopped; it explicitly covers every medication but Vitamin D2, so the carvedilol stop is kept with that upper bound.
The Discussion says the acidosis was at least in part controlled by hyperventilation, with a drop in pCO2; this is an author interpretation and no hyperventilation sign is recorded.
The Discussion cites a separate published case (Campbell and Liebman, stage 3 CKD, eGFR 45 to 74 mL/min after 4.5 months of a whole-food plant-based diet); it is not this patient and is excluded.

Table 1 prints the creatinine column header as "Creatinine(md/dL)", a one-character print artefact; the narrative gives the same values in mg/dL (5.08, 12.10, 2.78, 1.80 mg/dL). The Table 1 creatinine items record mg/dL and the measurement-series sidecar keeps the literal "md/dL"; this is an ambiguity, not a conflict.

The text calls the visit with the repeat labs "day 8" and cites Table 1, whose matching row is dated 22 May 2020; the text does not equate day 8 with a calendar date, the labs were sent on day 7, and the admission date and length of stay are not stated. The event keeps "day 8" and the lab items keep the table date.
